utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, on your way, did you pass through the convoy or through the crowd of refugees as you were walking to that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Kindly assist us and mark the place where that group or that crowd of refugees were, the one that you had to go through in order to get there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have to say I think that's outside the court's order and it's sort of an effort to open the door itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the relevance of this question to the nine bodies or ten bodies?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, I could answer by displaying the next clip, which was taken on the 12th of July at 1400 hours, that we have prepared for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then proceed and we'll see. So the question to you is whether you passed through the convoy or through a crowd of refugees as were you walking to that place. And you said you did, and then you were asked to mark the place where that group or that crowd of refugees were, in other words the group you had to go through in order to get there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This box here, this area, then up to Srebrenica, there were crowded people here, this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So could you put a Y next to that mark, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know that there is relevance but I asked to you state the relevance. Let's move to the next question or to the next document that you wish to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your assistance. And now can we bring up on e-court P01549, P01549. The photo is from the same collection. It is an aerial image that was taken on the 12th of July 1995 at 1400 hours, in other words in the afternoon, and this is relevant to the time that the witness is testifying about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, while the photo is being brought up, I would like to ask you something else. On the way to the place where the bodies were, did you see the transformation station? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Transformer station, power station.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the power plant?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know what it is. It's on the back of the "White House," we call it the "White House" it's on the back side of it, on the grass field or something, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You're looking at an image, an aerial image.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would kindly ask if this can be rotated clockwise so as to provide the witness with a better representation of the event, and can this also be lowered a little, please? Thank you. This will do. Sir, can you find your bearings on this photo and can you see across the road a black dot and the marking, "people"? Will you agree with me that this is the group of refugees that could be seen in this area at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yeah. It is possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you show us on this photo where it was that you turned westwards or where you turned right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: I think it was around here, this area, this area. You can see the path here also. It's a muddy path. It's up here, so up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that you passed before the group of refugees that is here, seen in this image?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes. But in that area, there were lots of refugees also so there were loads and loads of people, so I think this was a holdup for people but the buses were down there, more to the compound, so everywhere were people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And going on the route that you just marked, did you pass close to the transformer station or the power station that we just discussed a little while ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes. If I take this route, it's on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm going to finish up with a couple more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Are you finished with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. If you agree I would like to have the document marked now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you kindly, again, put PW-114 next to the mark that you see in red already, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you came to the place where you saw the bodies, were you able to identify any of those persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: No. I didn't see them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any identification documents next to the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: No. That's too far away and I was on the -- in an area with lots of trees so it was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know who these people were that were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: No, but I guess it were Muslims from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't want any guessing. Basically you either know or you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it were people from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And the next question follows logically: Why do you know this and you are not assuming that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: I never saw a civilian -- military in civilian clothes being killed before, and I assume that it's -- if you're making an attack like this you come in military units and not in civilian clothes so I know, and it were all civilians in civilian clothes so -- I'm a hundred per cent sure it were civilians from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could these have been civilians from Bratunac, Zelani Jadar, Potocari, or you are 100 per cent sure that they were from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yeah, from Srebrenica, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know who killed these people, if they were killed at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: I don't know who the people were but there were dead so they were not moving so I think they were dead, yeah. No, I don't think. I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was whether you know who killed them. You don't. All right. So for the record, the witness made a movement with his head indicating that he didn't -- he doesn't know. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you know when these people were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: No, I don't know the time. I was there at noon so it must be maybe on the 11th or on the 12th in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And to finish, is it possible that this incident took place on the 13th, the one that you're talking about today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: No, because I saw them on the 12th. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that the first day of the evacuation was the 12th of July and that the second day of the evacuation was the 13th of July, would that change anything of your conclusion about the date when you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to finish with the question: Do you abide by this still today, that this was on the second day of the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, on the second day of the evacuation, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you allow me to ask you just about the photographs that you mentioned today, can you please tell us how many bodies you photographed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Nine till ten and there were three pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to count in the photographs how many bodies there were, nine or ten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Not on the photos because the photos are from a bad quality, as you know. I saw them by myself and I counted them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thus your answer today about the number of the bodies is based on what you counted and not what you established later, on the photographs, because you have them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. We have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Madam Fauveau is representing General Miletic will now put some questions to you. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment because we are not receiving interpretation in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: A while ago my colleague read out to you a summary of what you said in the Krstic trial?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Go ahead. Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you heard this summary, you said that the summary tallied with what you had said in Krstic trial; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the summary, my colleague read out as follows: "[In English] In an area behind the 'White House' some 700 metres from the compound, the witness saw nine or ten corpses." [Interpretation] Is it fair to say that you did not mention this during the Krstic trial? Do you remember exactly what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: To assist you, I shall read back to you what you said during the Krstic trial. On page 1564. "[In English] Nine to ten corpses which I found were diagonally in an open field at the edge of a forest near a creek behind the interrogation house about 700 metres from the compound." [Interpretation] When you mentioned these corpses who you said you found them behind the interrogation house, you did not then mention the "White House," is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were there other things which were quite accurate in the summary which my colleague read out to you today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: It's all okay. It's same.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Which weren't quite accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you gave your first statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in September 1995, on 26 of September 1995, when you mentioned this interrogation house, you did say that this house was blue. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, we are going off the topic and in fairness, if the reason for that is about the summary I read, the counsel did not read an earlier part of his testimony where he talks about exactly what I said in the summary, calls it interrogation house, in a different part than the part she read there is a part, I can read it, I can read it in re-direct, which matches --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These are two issues in one brought together. Do proceed because it can be relevant or it might end up not being relevant at all, in which case we will stop you, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we show the witness Exhibit number 3D18, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That may need to be in private as well. It's his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I tried to download it myself to anticipate that. I anticipate that but it didn't work. So, yes, has this been broadcast or not yet? All right. So let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We are in open session, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that those bodies that you saw had clothes on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you remove these clothes in order to see the injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In that case, how were you able to see the wounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: They were covered with blood on the clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that you saw the blood stains and not the wounds themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: A wound of a shot is very small but the blood is mainly very big, so I don't see the wounds but the blood spots, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And was there a lot of blood on these clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, mostly on the back and in the main in the area of the head.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know the difference between an injury sustained by -- do you know the difference between an exit wound and an entry wound?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has already told you that he did not see the wounds themselves. What he the relevance of the question, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were you able to determine whether these bodies had been moved after their deaths?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: No, they never been moved. Afterwards, yeah, maybe, but when they have been shot, not, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What makes you come to that conclusion? How do you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They have been shot in the back and they just kept them there for a while and after I think when the -- all things were over they have been removed by a unit or something. I never been back there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: As you did not see the wounds, how do you know that these people were shot? How can you tell that these people were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: I think this is the most easiest way, and they were shooting all over the place, so this is most easy way and the fastest way.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that this is an assumption on your part rather than knowledge of the fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: I think it's a fact that it's the easy way to solve an issue very fast and quietly? Why to make lots of bombs and then to kill someone? It's easier and faster.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'm not asking you what's faster and what's easier. I'm just asking you how you can be so sure that these people were shot by a bullet, as you did not see the wounds.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: I think with a knife it's different. I think that -- that's my opinion but that's my private opinion. A bullet shot in the back it's easier from the distance and they cleared it off with a head shot to be sure that they were dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: How do you know that they had been shot in the back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Because I saw the blood spots from the back and they were lying with their head down, down in the stream.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when a bullet leaves a body, there is also blood, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes. There is. If you shoot a bullet inside a body, even shot, the first shot is going in the body, the hole is smaller than the out shot. The other side is bigger. So if you turn the body over, it's a big, mega hole. You don't want to see this.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But you did not see the other side. You only saw one side and you saw a lot of blood; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes. I saw enough, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Madam Fauveau. Mr. Josse? Mr. Josse is representing General Gvero here and he will be cross-examining you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could the witness be given a clean copy, so to speak, of P01516?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Now, witness, at page 1494 of your testimony in the Krstic case, you were asked various questions about where you saw Muslim fighters with mortars on the 11th of July in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the relevance of this to the nine bodies?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are -- without giving away my line of cross-examination, it goes to whether these killings were in fact opportunistic, as the Prosecution allege, or whether they could be described in some other manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's hear the rest of the questions, then, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And I want to be fair, I hope, because Mr. McCloskey, who was examining you at the time, showed you a diagram or photograph and asked you where you saw these fighters with the Muslims -- I beg your pardon, with the mortars, and you said, "Here, here, and here." And Mr. McCloskey said that "the record should indicate that he indicated he saw Muslim fighters on both sides of the UN base up in the hill area as well as the northern side of the UN base." I would like you to mark those areas on this plan, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: About here, here, here, I think here somewhere. Of course, they were running away, coming back, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: You mentioned in the testimony I have just read out, that they were on both sides of the UN base, so were they the other side as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: It was possible here in this area but when the Serbs came in they were running away so it was short basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And let's be clear about this. That was on the 11th of July, from your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: By the 12th of July, these people had run away into the woods because they were very nervous? I think you said that in fact in the passage I've just quoted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could you now mark where you saw the nine or ten bodies, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: In this area. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: So perhaps you would put by there nine bodies, by that line so we are clear.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the diagram, perhaps you would put, if this isn't unfair, Muslim fighters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Over here?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't forget the PW-114. You can put that top-left corner of the picture, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And on this plan, are you able to indicate from which side the Serb forces came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, from this side. And then went to this area, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And finally, I think, in which direction did the Muslim fighters flee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Should I mark it on the picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you mark that, let's mark these first, because they are too near where you put Muslim fighters before, and I don't want later on in a year or two from now to get confused. Next to the last two markings that you put on the left-hand side, could you put -- could you write, "Serb forces" and then draw an arrow straight, pointing to those two markings, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And just put an arrow. Okay. Now Mr. Josse has asked you to indicate on the map which direction the Muslim fighters fled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. For the record the witness indicates with two arrows, two arrows, on -- each on -- on each -- on either side of the building which appears in the middle of the picture. On top of each of those arrows could you just put "MF," please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to Your Honour and I've got nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Josse. Mr. Haynes is appearing for General Pandurevic and he will be asking you some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm not going to be very long with you. You very fairly described the circumstances in which you saw these bodies and the difficulties you had in seeing them or identifying them. In the summary of your evidence that was read out earlier, there was an approximation of the ages that you thought they were, and do you accept that any evidence that you can give about their ages is precisely that, an approximation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that the youngest of these bodies could very well have been 18, 19 or 20?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Haynes. Is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just one moment, Your Honour, one moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: A couple questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You were cross-examined about what you stated in Krstic about the location of the bodies and the summary. I want to refer you back to another part of your testimony in Krstic. This is on page 1528. Line 17. "Question: Where did you find the dead bodies?" "Answer: Behind the 'White House,' the interrogation house." A little further down: "Where is that? Behind the 'White House' about 700 metres from the compound is a kind of electrical house. I was familiar with this route because I had patrolled it many times." Now, when you say, "Behind the 'White House,'" are you referring to the bodies that you pound in the creek or were there other bodies actually right behind the white house, further away behind the "White House"? Does that, thinking back, is that -- are you -- do you stand by that testimony you made in Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes. It was the bodies that I found in the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. You were asked questions about the route you took when you found the bodies on the road. If you recall do you remember the name of that road, or did that road have a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: We called it the road, Buda-Pale, or Route 500, it was the name, the top of the hill was 500 metres so that's why.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry I said the bodies on the road. That's not correct. I mean the bodies you took -- the road you took when you found the bodies. Now I'd like to show you one of the photos you took. That's P02191. Maybe we can blow up a little bit the area between the white tape stripes. Maybe a little bit smaller, sorry. Okay. First of all, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you describe what is shown in the photograph between the white stripes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: There is a body lying, the man is wearing a blue vest with a white shirt underneath. He has black hair. He's lying down with his head in the stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just to be clear, could you take your pen and just draw a little arrow pointing to the head of this victim? Because, as you said, you had some difficulty with the quality of these photos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: This is his head, this here, this is his neck, this is his arm, shoulder, this is his blue vest, so his legs are here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. For the record, the markings the witness made go from left to right. He made a circle for the head --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: A number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We could do it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you please put a number 1 where you indicated the head of the victim is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think the rest is self explanatory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't need any further explanations. No, thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, could you please put PW-114 in the corner of this and then we can save it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-114
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, we don't have any further questions for you which basically means that your testimony finishes here. On behalf of the Trial Chamber and also of the Tribunal, I wish to thank you for having come again to this Tribunal to give evidence once more. And we wish you a safe journey back to where you are going.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You'll be escorted and given the assistance you require. Do we need to draw the curtains down or not? If we have the break now, let's draw the curtain because there is something I need to discuss with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next witness, PW-112, I just want to make sure where we stand. We ordered his protective measures on the 23rd of August 2006; is that correct? All right. Did we assign to him the pseudonym then or not? Because he had testified under protective measures before. So those he carries with him, but I'm not quite sure that we assigned the PW-112 to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. We assigned that number to him and that is in the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then we have no further obstacles. The other thing -- let's go into private session for one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's thrash this straight away. Documents to be tendered or that are being tendered by the Prosecution in relation to the previous witness, PW-114?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. P02270 is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Right, under seal, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it there is no objection. Yes, so that is being admitted and it will be preserved under seal. Next is what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: PIC 00030, P02191, that was the thing that was marked by the witness. The photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. I hear no objection. So it is so admitted. And, of course, admitted also would be the documents that were referred to in his testimony as per our previous decision but we don't need to go into detail. Defence for Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We would like the two photos to be admitted, the witness did use them, 4DIC 27 and 4DIC 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So it's 4DI -- 4DIC 27 and 4DIC 28. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, but I would point out that one of those photos, I don't remember which one, was dated 12 July and the witness clearly said it was day 2 that he went to see the bodies so that 12 July photo wasn't so relevant but he said 12 July so we didn't object but if everyone understands that, we -- we'll allow it in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that but I don't think we need an explanation from Mr. Stojanovic because it's clear enough. So there is no objection as such so both documents are tendered, are being admitted and marked accordingly, as I stated. The -- Mr. Josse, you wish to tender, I suppose, IC29?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So it's 6DIC29. No objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. There are no further documents that you wish to tender, Mr. Ostojic or Ms. Fauveau? None. Okay. Thank you. So we can proceed now with the next witness. In the case of this witness we don't have any Rule 92 bis --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps while this is going down just one matter to help save some time, in the 13 July 2006, your order, you granted us leave to put in evidence of the Snagovo executions but you said no evidence on those executions for six months until the -- after the trial started. We have two Snagovo -- the two Snagovo witnesses ready for next week. I've asked counsel if they had any problems. They don't. But we did find your order and thought, of course, we best --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If there is no objection, then we can proceed. I just want a confirmation from the Defence teams that there --

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that you agree. All right. So then you will -- you can proceed accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also have been told that you are in a position to feed the Trial Chamber back on the motion that is I referred to earlier on, just before the break. Yes, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We are in a position to respond to the submission that was filed for the witnesses that are supposed to arrive as of Monday after the 30th of October. The Defence has been consulted and we don't have any objections to the witness 54 being granted protective measures as opposed to witness 50. We believe the argument is that the Prosecution has provided to the Trial Chamber and we fully agree with the Chamber's decision on granting protective measures for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will eventually hand down an oral decision on this. In the meantime, you have the position of the Defence teams very clear, and you know where you stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon or good evening to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And on behalf of the Tribunal, I wish to welcome you to this trial, where you are going to give evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have given evidence before, and more or less you are familiar with the procedure. Madam Usher is going to give you the text of a solemn declaration that is required from you before you start your evidence. That is a solemn declaration that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking testifying the truth. So please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn commitment with this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you, sir. Could you kindly take a seat and I'll explain two brief matters. First of all, the Prosecution on your behalf asked that you continue enjoying protective measures in this case. We know that you had protective measures before when you testified in this Tribunal. We have kept them. We have granted the Prosecution's request, so you will be testifying under these conditions: First, your identity will be hidden from the public. You will be referred to as Witness PW-112. Of course, some lawyers may address you as witness or as sir. But for us, you are Witness PW-112. And no one will refer to you by name. Second is that we have agreed to grant you what are referred to as facial distortion here. Facial distortion basically means that anyone outside these four walls will not be able to see your face while you are testifying. Anyone who will be following these proceedings will be able to see a Melange of squares, coloured squares, but not your face. Also, in certain -- at certain moments, there may be the need to go into private session for the same purpose of not revealing your identity. When we go into private session, basically it means that what is being said can only be heard inside these -- this courtroom, not outside. So no one would be able to follow the proceedings for the entire time when we are in private session. Is that to your satisfaction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So who will be leading the -- yes, so first there is going to be examination-in-chief by Mr. Vanderpuye, correct me if I don't pronounce your name well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Afterwards, that won't happen today for sure, you will be cross-examined by the various Defence teams. Please try to keep your answers as brief as possible, and when a question is put to you that can be answered with a yes or no, just give a yes or no answer unless you need -- you feel the need to explain further. Have I been clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for being patient with us. We need to finish today at quarter to 7, not at 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good evening, Your Honours ladies and gentlemen I would ask that the pseudonym sheet P22070 be shown to the witness:

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness if he is the person named in that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. I just want to make sure one of the Defence teams has a look at the document, and let us have a look at it. I take it, as before, that you're satisfied that Mr. Meek has seen the document. Okay. All right. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to apprise the Court of my initial intention to introduce the prior testimony of this witness pursuant to 92 ter. I intend obviously to lay the necessary foundation to do that but I wanted to first, obviously, ask permission to do that. Secondly to advise the Court that it's my intention to read a relatively brief summary of the witness's prior testimony into the record so that -- so as to orient the Court to the witness's testimony for purposes of cross-examination, further direct-examination, which I also intend to conduct. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's take it up from here straight away. Does anyone of you Defence teams doubt the existence of all the requirements for the application of Rule 92 ter? The witness is present. He's available for cross-examination and questioning by us. We only need to see whether he is in a position to give the attestation that is mentioned in that rule. Any objections to the admittance of his previous testimony under Rule 92 ter? I hear no objections. So you have the authorisation provided that he proceeds with the appropriate attestation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well, Judge. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, may I ask, do you recall having testified in the matter of the Prosecutor versus Radislav Krstic, a proceeding before there Tribunal on the 23rd of May, the year of 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are allowing it today and I can understand of course the position of the Defence teams in saying no problem with us, because they would have had available already the transcript of the witness's testimony in those previous trials but we have not had that luxury. We only get to see the transcripts when we have admitted them. So the unfortunate part of it is that we are going to start with this witness now without having read what he stated -- what he's testified in the other cases. We are allowing it because basically this is Friday, we have got another 17 minutes left and we can read the transcript over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I greatly appreciate that. I do have the summary though that hopefully will orient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the summary is a summary so I think once it is admitted we have the right to read it through.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So in future, we would pretty much agree that you try to admit as many transcripts and statements under Rule 92 ter as much as possible but at least do give us prior, advance notice, of it so that we can procure a copy of the transcripts and be prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I do apologise to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not criticising you. I'm just saying for the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I don't want to be unduly difficult and indeed it's not me who is going to be cross-examining the witness. However, we can't locate the summary that my learned friend is referring to. Has it been distributed? I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it hasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's most unsatisfactory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is an 11th hour -- as I see it, this is an 11th hour decision that has been taken to seek the admittance of the previous transcript of the testimony under Rule 92 ter here, within the sitting itself. You were unprepared for it. We were unprepared for it. But obviously Mr. Vanderpuye, on the assumption that it would be granted, has prepared a summary but we haven't seen it and you haven't seen it. That's how I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Judge, I do apologise to my learned colleague. I was not aware there was a disclosure requirement with respect to the summary of a prior transcribed testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not a disclosure requirement. It's a question of courtesy more than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that, and I do apologise to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Mr. Josse, once -- I want to be fair to everyone, once you've raised the matter, do you have any objection to us proceeding?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We don't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate that. And anyone else from the Defence. Let's proceed. Mr. Lazarevic, yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, basically I don't have problem with admitting prior statements of this witness, but I would like on behalf of couple of other Defences that I have consulted just a moment ago, to pose two questions. This is not cross-examination. These are just two procedural questions to the witness directly, before we proceed with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's put it like this. Tell the Trial Chamber what you want to know and presumably whether you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first question is whether this witness speaks English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And what's the other question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Whether he had opportunity to read his previous transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think they are two very valid questions. We are not allowing you to put them directly to him because I don't think that's proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But of course Your Honour, I think it's the best way to address the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Point taken. Two very valid issues that you have raised. Will you deal with them yourself, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I certainly intend to, Judge. That appears to me to be a foundational issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is, yeah. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe you indicated, Mr. Witness, that you recalled testifying in the matter of the Prosecutor versus Krstic on the 23rd of May 2000; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And on the day that you testified, did you testify under the designated name Witness S?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was the testimony that you offered on that day truthful?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you will an opportunity to have the transcript of your testimony read back to you in a language that you speak and understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was that in the language in which you originally gave your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What language is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the course of your having reviewed the transcript of your prior testimony, did you indicate that it contained certain errors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were the errors as follows: Did you -- did you make a reference to your testimony having contained the term "a ticket"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Term "ticket," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. And for the purposes of the Court, and I do apologise since you don't have a transcript, that refers to the transcript page 3246, lines 19 through 22. And is that reference to your having had a ticket correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: I don't know which ticket you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall having had read back to you a passage in your testimony in which there was an indication that you had a ticket which you had for work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall having been read back a reference to a village by the name of "Ragacici"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall making a reference to a village by the name of "Ragacici" in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Ragacici, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you make a reference to the village by the name of "Magasici"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Magasici, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that the correct reference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Where we passed, yes, Magasici.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. For the purpose of the record that reference is contained on transcript page 3267, line 18. And sir, do you recall being read back a reference to an individual by the name of Salih Hasanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Hasan Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that the correct reference with respect to that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. For the record that is indicated on page 3266, line 17 of the prior transcript. Sir, aside from these errors, does the transcript fairly and accurately reflect the testimony that you gave on that date, that is the 23rd of May, 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does that transcript fairly and accurately reflect what you would say were you to be examined today and asked those same questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would move to have the transcript admitted under seal as an exhibit in this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, Your Honours, may it please the Tribunal, the Trial Chamber, I don't know that there is foundation that the witness has testified today, he has stated that he would say if examined these items, these particular items, but I don't think there has been foundation from this witness that his entire testimony, the transcript that they would like admitted, is accurate and if examined today he would restate all of those things that he testified to previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Basically Mr. Meek is suggesting that your question was not comprehensive enough and that it should be particularised to what he's just mentioned. In other words, we want to know from you, sir, if you were asked all the same questions that you were asked when you gave testimony in Krstic, would you answer exactly the same, except for these discrepancies, or would your answers be different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They would be the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They would be the same. Does it satisfy you now, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Basically if I can just add something to what Mr. Meek said, I cannot interfere in the proceedings that Prosecution has with witnesses and preparing witnesses, but according to my knowledge, there is an existing video evidence of there and every other witness so perhaps the Trial Chamber could see before we agree with the admittance of his previous statement whether something of this kind was shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps we can cover that. Mr. Vanderpuye asked you whether the transcript of your previous testimony was translated to you in your own language, and you answered yes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who translated the transcript to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And were you also shown the video recording of your testimony in Krstic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean the picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe I can answer that, judge. I believe and perhaps the witness can correct me if I'm wrong that the picture he's referring to is actually the exhibits relating to his testimony that was given in the prior proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the thing is that when he says that the transcript of his testimony was read out to him in his own language, basically, it is physical reading out of the transcript in his own language and not viewing the --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- video recording. And there was no viewing of the video recording itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe the witness can answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, he has to answer it. There was no viewing of the video recording of your testimony, of your previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is correct. I just viewed the exhibit, and I read my testimony and then there were a few -- a couple of mistakes that I corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think that clarifies the matter completely. I see that Mr. Lazarevic is also -- seems to be also content with that. So it's move. We've got another three minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, to be honest, judge, I don't think I can get through the summary in two or three minutes, but I did want to clarify the record on one issue relating to the witness's having heard his testimony. If I may put a question to the witness in that regard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, was it the case that an individual read to you your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: No. I read it myself.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the second part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you make use of an interpreter when you reviewed your testimony in the -- on May the 20th -- 23rd of 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So were you -- in other words let's get this clear. Were you provided an entire copy of your testimony in Krstic in the Serbo-Croat language or in the Bosnian language? Or was it in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I read it in Bosnian, and I noticed a couple of mistakes like the name Salih Hasanovic instead of -- well, we just corrected it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, there is a -- one thing that you need to do, Mr. Vanderpuye, because our staff will be gone. We've only got one left. We need the copy of this transcript which is not yet in e-court, I suppose. Is it? Then please -- we won't be able to access it from home. So the case manager of the Prosecution, if you could kindly e-mail the transcript to each one of us so that we can read it over the weekend? Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours, the way I understand this, there is a transcript in B/C/S. Our clients have not been provided with that. We've asked for this on many occasions especially with there kind of a witness. We didn't object to them doing this in the spirit of goodwill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine this was translated purposely for this witness. They don't translate transcripts into --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Judge, I think Mr. Meek is -- I won't say he's mistaken because the record speaks for itself, but I believe that there is either a translation error or the witness is has misapprehended the questions that have been put to him. With respect to the statement that he's read --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I don't want my learned friend to give evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're 100 per cent right, Mr. Josse. Let's leave it at this. We'll take it up on Monday morning and not in front of the witness. All right? Not in front of the witness. Now, sir, we will continue on Monday morning. You have a long weekend to rest during which time you are not to communicate or allow anyone to communicate with you on the subject matter of your testimony. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So we'll meet again Monday morning at 9.00. Have a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 30th day of October, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: WITNESS:  EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.47 p.m.,
